observations: Bitmap smoke displayed the title, repainted, automatically closed and returned to Program Manager without a guest fault.
Forced starfield smoke displayed the Stars! lettering, sparse stars and four buttons, then repainted and closed without a guest fault.
Alt+N and Alt+O each displayed the expected milestone notice; Enter dismissed each notice and restored the artwork. Alt+X closed cleanly.
A separate launch closed cleanly with Alt+F4.
The original executable displayed the same title artwork and version text under the same running display setup, and closed with Alt+X.
The original Continue button was enabled; the isolated reconstruction Continue button was disabled. This is expected because their startup settings are separate.
No obvious title-screen corruption or PROGMAN fault was observed during these checks.
The user independently confirmed that the graphical artifacts were not happening in this run.
limits: Earlier PROGMAN/USER.EXE fault remains unexplained (U023); non-reproduction does not identify or eliminate its cause.
This was a visual comparison, not a captured-image pixel comparison.
Forced fallback uses the 256-color guest to exercise the alternate drawing branch; it is not acceptance on a real 16-color display driver.
Tests used keyboard controls; mouse automation and other resolutions/font settings were not validated.
The original fallback caller context remains open (U022).
Full application startup/configuration, creation/loading and main game UI remain incomplete.
